messages:
taylor_csm: Heads-up: QBR next week for Vega Labs. I dug into their spend — embeddings up 3x last month, and a couple of new feature flags that might be generating heavy token churn. We should align on a short playbook for cost mitigation and renewal signals.
ajay_finops: Thanks — can you drop the rough numbers? do we have top endpoints or routes? :eyes:
taylor_csm: Quick snapshot: avg daily tokens went from 2.1M -> 6.8M over last 30 days. Top 3 routes: /embed/bulk, /chat/assistant, /search-rerank. Most of the spike correlates with an onboarding campaign that enabled client-side batching but set batch size to 1 accidentally.
maria_onboard: Oh yikes — that batching bug rings a bell. I handed a rollout doc to Vega last month. I can ask them to revert to the controlled rollout flag today.
jenna_se: Also flagged for renewal in 45 days. If spend stays this high they'll hit commit thresholds and request a discount — classic risk. We should propose immediate temp throttles + a plan to optimize.
ajay_finops: Proposal: 1) add short-term guardrail in prod: rate-limit heavy routes to 60% of current baseline for 72h, 2) enable prefix KV cache for chat where applicable, 3) run targeted quantization on the 2nd model variant, 4) cost-shared alert to Vega with suggested knobs. Anything missing?
taylor_csm: Also capture qualitative feedback: why did they change batching? was it deliberate? need to document for renewal conversation. I'll DM their eng lead.
maria_onboard: I'll surface a one-pager on best-practice batching + sample code for client-side grouping. small snippet we can paste: ```js
// recommended batching
const group = []; // group messages until size >= 16 or timeout
// send grouped request to /embed/bulk
```
budget-bot: alert: Vega Labs daily tokens 2026-03-18 = 6.8M (+220%). Threshold breach: >= 5M for 3 consecutive days. Notified owners: taylor_csm, ajay_finops.
ajay_finops: I'll draft the alert message we'll send to Vega — transparent, with suggested mitigations and rollback steps. want to keep it collaborative, not punitive.
jenna_se: For the QBR deck: include current run rate, projected 30/60/90 day spend under three scenarios (status quo, conservative throttle, optimized). Also show expected MMR impact and renewal levers (commit restructure, feature gate timing).
taylor_csm: Action items: + maria = send batching one-pager to Vega today, + ajay = draft alert + 30/60/90 spend model by EOD, + jenna = draft renewal talking points and pricing options, + me = confirm rollback flag with Vega eng. I'll post a follow-up thread with the short playbook.
maria_onboard: On it — will attach code examples and a quick checklist for their SDKs.
ajay_finops: Putting numbers into the sheet now. If anyone wants to eyeball the model, link: https://go.redwood/rev-spend-model (internal)
jenna_se: Great. If we get Vega to accept a 14-day controlled throttle and optimize batching, we can probably shave 40-60% off the surge within a week. That should stabilize renewal posture.
taylor_csm: Perfect. Let's reconvene 24h after alerts go out. Thanks all :thumbsup:
